original_value: It is proposed a novel instantaneous frequency estimation technology, multi-generalized demodulation transform, for non-stationary signals, whose true time variations of instantaneous frequencies are unknown and difficult to extract from the time-frequency representation due to essentially noisy environment. Theoretical bases of the novel instantaneous frequency estimation technology are created. The main innovations are summarized as: (a) novel instantaneous frequency estimation technology, multi-generalized demodulation transform, is proposed, (b) novel instantaneous frequency estimation results, obtained by simulation, for four types of amplitude and frequency modulated non-stationary single and multicomponent signals under strong background noise (signal to noise ratio is −5 dB), and (c) novel experimental instantaneous frequency estimation results for defect frequency of rolling bearings for multiple defect frequency harmonics, using the proposed technology in non-stationary conditions and in conditions of different levels of noise interference, including a strong noise interference. Quantitative instantaneous frequency estimation errors are employed to evaluate performance of the proposed IF estimation technology. Simulation and experimental estimation results show high effectiveness of the proposed estimation technology.

result.paraphrase: A novel instantaneous frequency estimation technique, the multi-generalized demodulation transform, is proposed for non-stationary signals whose true instantaneous-frequency variations are unknown and hard to recover from the time-frequency representation in a strongly noisy environment. Theoretical foundations for this new IF estimation method are established. The main contributions are: (a) the proposed multi-generalized demodulation transform as a new IF estimation technology, (b) simulation-based IF estimation results for four kinds of amplitude- and frequency-modulated non-stationary single- and multicomponent signals under strong background noise (signal-to-noise ratio of −5 dB), and (c) experimental IF estimation results for rolling-bearing defect frequencies with multiple defect-frequency harmonics, obtained with the proposed method under non-stationary conditions and at different noise-interference levels, including strong noise interference. Quantitative IF estimation errors are used to assess the method’s performance. Both simulation and experimental results demonstrate the high effectiveness of the proposed estimation technique.
